To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Using web data to augment training data and a small set of real training data to perform domain adaptation improves object classification performance for real data.”

we are able to improve the classification accuracy of a classifier for 3D scans of urban environments by using web data and that we are able for the first time to perform domain adaptation for 3D data.

(1) data from the 3d warehouse are a good source of additional training data for object recognition, (2) domain adaptation is a good method for adapting data from different domains and (3) the combination of both methods significantly improves classification accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two important aspects in robotics, the use of web data and the use of unlabeled data.
the following questions: (1) How can we use the World Wide Web to obtain training data for object recognition in robotics?
how to use web data to improve classification of 3D laser data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our domain adaptation approach can significantly improve the classification accuracy of a 3D laser scan classifier when only little labeled real data are available.
our approach is able to improve the classification accuracy of 3D laser point clouds by more than 10% in comparison to a classifier that was trained on real data alone.
our approach allows us to train a classifier for the recognition of objects in 3D laser scan data with only a small set of manually labeled training data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to classify 3D laser scan data from an autonomous vehicle into 10 classes (e.g. car, building, road) with a classification accuracy of 80% using only 100 training examples.
it provides a way of leveraging web resources in order to reduce the amount of manually labeled training data needed to train a 3D laser scan classifier for a new object category.
the use of web data and domain-adaptation can reduce the need for manual annotation of training data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to significantly reduce the effort needed to collect training data by using the web.
web data can be used as an additional source of data to improve object recognition.
it is possible to leverage web data to train classifiers for objects in the real world.
